_note: PEP-OWNED execution catalog for certification planning. It COMPOSES with configuration/containers_list.json (the authoritative platform source: that file owns which concrete containers, per architecture, are currently enabled/runnable). This file adds ONLY the three things the container list cannot express and that are genuinely certification policy: (1) supported_pg_majors — the PG majors PEP can currently execute for certification; (2) platforms — the bridge from a packaging OS token (as the detector/cert-plan emit it) to the container catalog's OS identities (catalog_os), where a container alias is '<catalog_os>-<arch>'; (3) certification_counterparts — an explicit, certification-only opt-in for implicit opposite-arch containers (container_resolver counterparts of an ENABLED physical entry, for a mapped catalog_os), added one alias at a time once a probe has proven the exact package on that platform. Counterparts are never physical containers_list.json entries, so the regression workflow's default and 'all' selections do not change; the planner fails closed if one is unknown, physical, unmapped, duplicated or no longer has an enabled sibling. It never duplicates the arch or enabled state of a physical container, and it is NOT a fixed cell universe. Retire an OS by removing its platforms entry here (or disabling its containers in containers_list.json); add PG majors or platforms as data, no code change. Debian bullseye is intentionally ABSENT because it is EOL: historical bullseye build evidence therefore surfaces as an explicit unsupported coverage gap instead of silently disappearing. debian11 may remain enabled in containers_list.json for regression, but certification does not run on EOL bullseye.
